description: I'm an information engineering student at Fukuyama University, Japan, interested in how data can help people make decisions. I'm taking on Field Shift as a solo participant. With THE NEXT SEED, I plan to use NASA Earth observation data to explore how limited irrigation water and the cost of switching crops can change which crop rotations farmers can choose.
summary: THE NEXT SEED helps farmers near Ames, Iowa, explore whether to add winter cereal rye between corn and soybean. It uses NASA POWER rainfall data to show when to recheck field moisture and uses field observations and spring work constraints to help compare two rotation options.
details:
THE NEXT SEED compares two crop rotations at a reference location near Ames, Iowa. It uses NASA POWER rainfall data to compare March–May totals with the 2001–2020 median. In the demo, switching from 2024 to the lower-rainfall spring of 2023 adds a prompt to recheck field moisture if conditions become drier.
Users enter observed soil moisture, erosion concerns, their management priority, and whether they can terminate rye in spring. Reported dry soil prompts a field review before choosing rye. If spring termination is unavailable, the app highlights the baseline corn–soybean rotation and, where erosion is a concern, suggests discussing soil conservation options that fit the farm’s available operations.
The prototype uses HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. It covers one reference location and has yet to be validated on working farms.
dataRefs: NASA POWER — Monthly Corrected Precipitation (PRECTOTCORR, MERRA-2)
projectRefs: Iowa State University Extension — Post Corn, Going to Soybean: Use Cereal Rye
